messages:
sasha: Quick sync — I'm working on locking the prompt/prefix caching contract for the public API. Main questions: what exactly goes into the cache key, how do we surface cache headers, and how do we handle invalidation/backcompat when keys change? cc @mai @devon @priya

mai: Can you list the invariants you're trying to preserve? e.g., identical model+prefix+prompt should always HIT (if not evicted). Also is this for shared (global) cache or per-customer caches?

sasha: Good point. Target invariants: 1) For hosted shared cache we want deterministic hits for semantically identical requests (after normalization). 2) We must avoid leaking PII in cache keys/headers. 3) Changing non-semantic metadata (client_request_id, trace_id) should not change key.

devon: Current runtime key composition (prototype) is: `model|model_version|prefix_hash|prompt_norm|response_schema_version`. We purposely excluded sampling params so deterministic responses can be cached. Question: do we include `user_id` for dedicated customers? currently we don't for hosted.

priya: Sampling params convo: if `temperature` or `top_p` differ the output will diverge. My take: by default do NOT include sampling params in key and only allow caching when a request sets `deterministic=true` (or `sampling=null`). Otherwise the cache is bypassed.

mai: Sounds reasonable. For dedicated/private deployments customers may want per-tenant isolation. Let's ensure key has an optional tenant namespace prefix when in Dedicated mode. Implementation: runtime uses `tenant_id || 'shared'` as leading namespace.

devon: For header surface, proposal: Response headers: `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600, stale-while-revalidate=60` (configurable per route), and `X-Redwood-Cache: HIT|MISS`. For debugging we can add `X-Redwood-Cache-Hint: <short-hash>` but not the raw key. No PII in hint.

cache-bot: reminder — plumbing PRs should include tests for header presence and hit/miss semantics.

sasha: Agree on `X-Redwood-Cache`. One more: do we include the prompt prefix version in the key? i.e., when customers update a prefix template we might want to invalidate. Proposal: include `prefix_version` (int) in key. That lets us avoid global purges when templates change.

priya: That works. Also propose a safety TTL + versioning: TTL default 1 hour, but we always allow explicit purge API to remove specific prefix hashes or bump `prefix_version`. For big infra changes we can bump a global `cache_schema` number to force full backcompat invalidation.

devon: Example key composition (hash input):

```
key_input = concat(tenant_namespace, "|", model, "|", model_version, "|", prefix_version, "|", prefix_hash, "|", normalized_prompt)
key = sha256(key_input)
```

Normalization notes: trim whitespace, fold unicode, remove ephemeral session tokens embedded in prompt (we need a sanitizer).

mai: Backcompat checklist: 1) When we change key_input we must increment `cache_schema` and publish migration notes. 2) Console and SDK should surface `X-Redwood-Cache-Hint` so customers can report misses. 3) Add FAQ in docs about which request fields affect caching.

sasha: On response body metadata: we should NOT include the full cache key in body, but we can include a small `cache_debug` object with `hit: true/false` and `hint: <hex>` and `ttl_remaining: seconds`. Those are helpful for debugging but ensure we sanitize.

devon: Implementation tasks: I'll add header emission and TTL config in runtime (PR target EOD Tue). Priya — can you add e2e that asserts deterministic=true caches and sampling params bypass cache? Mai — will update docs with the cache contract and header list. Sasha — I'll need a list of fields that are considered non-cache-affecting; I can put a linter in the SDK to warn if those fields are present in key-critical places.

priya: Tests will include: 1) identical prompt+prefix -> HIT within TTL, 2) different temperature -> MISS unless deterministic flag set, 3) bump prefix_version -> MISS, 4) tenant namespace isolates keys for Dedicated.

mai: One open question: prefetching / warm cache semantics. If a client asks for `prefetch=true` we should allow the runtime to write a cache entry but mark it with a shorter `prefetch_ttl` and set header `X-Redwood-Cache: PREFETCHED`. That avoids confusing metrics. Thoughts?

sasha: Nice: `PREFETCHED` vs `HIT` vs `MISS` is clear. Also include `Cache-Control: s-maxage=<prefetch_ttl>` for CDN-aware caching. Make sure prefetch writes respect tenant isolation.

devon: Also, do we want to allow partial-key caching (prefix-only cache) where we cache only the prefix expansion result so it can be reused across prompts? That's more complex; maybe a follow-up RFC. For now, keep single-entry cache per full prompt+prefix.

priya: Agreed — keep simple for launch. Follow-up: explore prefix-component caching (expensive template rendering) later.

sasha: Next steps: I'll open an RFC PR documenting key composition, headers (`Cache-Control`, `X-Redwood-Cache`, `X-Redwood-Cache-Hint`), invalidation APIs, and the `deterministic` flag rule. Devon to implement runtime header + key hashing. Priya to add tests. Mai to update docs/FAQ. Can we aim to merge all by next Wed? :thumbsup:

mai: Yep. I'll carve out docs PR this week.

devon: I'll add a small debug endpoint that returns `X-Redwood-Cache-Hint` for a given request (only to internal teams). Will include feature flag.

sasha: Great. Thanks all. If anyone sees blocking issues ping me here.

cache-bot: scheduled reminder — add perf dashboard tiles for cache hit-rate and average latency for HIT vs MISS.
